patch_description:
Replace the random Gaussian cloud with a symmetric 14-point cube–octahedron compound. The eight cube vertices and six coordinate-axis vertices provide a much more uniform diameter-bounded packing than random points.

The axis radius is chosen as `sqrt(3)`, equal to the cube circumradius. This keeps the maximum distance at the cube diameter while maximizing the limiting cube-to-axis distance within this symmetric family. The resulting configuration has a deterministic squared minimum/maximum ratio of approximately `(6 - 2*sqrt(3)) / 12 = 0.2113`, vastly improving on an unconstrained random sample, while returning exactly a finite `(14, 3)` NumPy array.
